sources.entry: Arroxy - Video and audio downloader powered by yt-dlp, with a built-in browser, playlists, subtitles and download profiles.

summary.one_liner: Arroxy is a free, GPLv3-licensed desktop downloader for YouTube and 2000+ sites, built on yt-dlp, with an in-app browser (Explore) that can use your own sign-in to fetch videos your account can access.
summary.what_it_does: Arroxy downloads video and audio from YouTube and more than 2000 other sites via yt-dlp, with ffmpeg handling muxing. Its Explore tab is a built-in browser where you can browse a site and download the video, playlist, or channel you are viewing, or right-click a link to download it. You can sign in once in Explore so downloads can reach content your account can watch, such as private videos and Watch Later or Liked lists. The app supports reusable download profiles (format, resolution, subtitles, filename template), a parallel download queue with pause, retry and priority, and bulk URL paste. It can also download only a time range or chapter, export audio-only as MP3, M4A, Opus or WAV, and handle subtitles in SRT, VTT or ASS. Playlist sync and an .m3u file are included.
use_cases: Download a YouTube video or playlist to local disk
Grab private or age-restricted videos from my own account
Extract audio as MP3 or M4A from a video
Batch download subtitles for a playlist
Archive videos from sites beyond YouTube
Save only a chapter or time range of a video
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <url> | sh -s -- --appimage (Linux AppImage; URL missing from the README text)
bun run bootstrap && bun run dev
notable: Explore browser lets you sign in once and download content your account can access, without exporting cookies
Per-item playlist profiles let one playlist pass save some videos as 8K and others as audio only
Explicitly marks AI-upscaled streams and skips them unless allowed
Global hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+D / Cmd+Shift+D) queues a copied link without opening the window
caveats: Windows and macOS builds are not code-signed, so SmartScreen and Gatekeeper show warnings on first launch; macOS needs a Terminal xattr command for the DMG route
Linux release downloads are x86_64 only; the Flatpak fails on ARM64 machines
Some features are listed as roadmap items only (date-range filters, scheduled downloads, AUR package)
Using an account for downloads carries some risk of that account being restricted, per the README
